match.reason: The bank point covers energy systems in movement science, not the nutrient fats (their roles in storing energy, insulating and aiding vitamin absorption, or the healthier unsaturated versus saturated and trans fats), so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Fats
card: Fats store energy for the body to use later. They also insulate the body, which helps keep heat in, and they help absorb some vitamins, such as A, D, E and K.
Unsaturated
fats found in foods such as olive oil, avocado, nuts and oily fish. They are the healthier choice.
Saturated
fats found in foods such as butter, fatty meat and many pastries. Eating a lot of them is less healthy.
Trans
fats made in some processed foods and found in small amounts in some animal foods. They are also less healthy than unsaturated fats.
draft.remember: Fats store energy, insulate and help absorb some vitamins. Choose unsaturated fats most often.

a.q: Which food is a good source of unsaturated fat?
a.why: Avocado contains unsaturated fat, which is the healthier type. Butter is mostly saturated fat, so it is less healthy.
a.clue: Think of a plant food, not a dairy or meat food.

b.q: Priya wants to swap one cooking fat for a healthier one. Which swap is best?
opts: Avocado replaced with a fatty meat
b.why: Olive oil is mostly unsaturated, so swapping butter for it lowers saturated fat. The other swaps move from an unsaturated fat to a saturated one, which is the wrong direction.
b.clue: Which swap moves towards unsaturated fat?

problems.detail: The clue 'Think of a plant food, not a dairy or meat food' gives the answer away. Avocado is the only plant food among the options, so a student can pick it without knowing which fats are unsaturated.
The option 'Avocado replaced with a fatty meat' does not fit the stem, which asks about swapping a cooking fat. Neither avocado nor fatty meat is a cooking fat, so the distractor is confusing.
